All six candidates are real. Two are major and should be fixed before this lands: #0 (GoogleOAuthService.acceptInviteToken is a third invite-redemption path never enrolled in the round-1 removed-customer gate, so a removed customer's invite still activates via Google sign-in and burns the token) and #1 (the daily license-expiry sweep still pushes, emails and SMSes removed customers — the B131 symptom class through a fourth cron, refuting the plan's two-cron sweep claim). Two are major and belong in the same fix round as findings already open: #0 (GoogleOAuthService.acceptInviteToken redeems a removed customer's invite and destroys the token — the Google twin of the acceptInvite/requestSeller gap, missed despite the round-2 edit in the same file) and #1 (authorization-expiry.runExpirySweep is the third customer-reaching @LeaderCron and still sends to removed customers, metered to the seller — B131's own class, established by a full sweep of the 13 pinned jobs). The fixer should apply the same customer.deletedAt refusal to #0 and #1 (with a REG spec each, and a skipped-count in the expiry cron summary consistent with the open cron-summary finding), add deletedAt checks to the two schedule create() methods and the third orders branch, and amend the build-plan Sibling notes. findings.detail: State path: (1) seller invites customer C → CustomerLink{status:INVITED, inviteToken:T, customerId:C}; (2) seller removes C → Customer.deletedAt set, link untouched (customers.service.ts:2045-2046, soft branch writes only deletedAt + User INACTIVE — verified); (3) the buyer completes Google sign-in with T in the OAuth state (web/buyer/invite/[token]/page.tsx:123 puts invite_token in the /auth/google query; auth.controller.ts:226→244 forwards it; google-oauth.service.ts:178 embeds it in state; :334 reads it back; :609-611 calls acceptInviteToken). acceptInviteToken (:643-664) reads `customerLink.findFirst({ where: { inviteToken: token, status: { in: ["INVITED","PENDING_SELLER_APPROVAL"] } } })` at :647 with NO `customer: { deletedAt: null }` — its own comment at :645 claims it "Mirrors BuyerService.acceptInvite's gate", which round 1 amended to carry exactly that filter (buyer.service.ts:120 per the digest) — and then WRITES at :653-661 `{ buyerAccountId, status: "ACTIVE", inviteToken: null, inviteExpiresAt: null, linkedAt: now }`. Consequences, all verified in code: (a) a removed customer's link goes ACTIVE, the write R6 and the round-1 fence amendment exist to prevent (the plan records only customers.service.ts approveBuyerRequest as an out-of-fence twin, and google-oauth.service.ts was admitted INTO scope by the round-2 amendment); (b) the invite token is nulled, which restore cannot undo — the seller must mint a new invite, so it is not restore-symmetric; (c) the same request then computes the newly-filtered `sellerCount` at :618 → 0, while auth.controller.ts:337 sets `linked: profile.inviteToken ? "true" : "false"` unconditionally, so the callback (web/(auth)/auth/google/callback/page.tsx:147) sends the buyer to /buyer/portal?linked=true and portal/page.tsx:332-360 shows "Seller connected successfully. Welcome!" over a seller list that getSellers now hides. Reachability beyond the race (page loaded while C was live, seller removes C during the Google round-trip, or a tab left open): GET /api/v1/auth/google?tenant=<slug>&context=portal&invite_token=<T> is unauthenticated, so a buyer holding their own emailed token can re-redeem it after removal.

findings.summary: A fourth customer-owned daily cron keeps contacting removed customers by push, email and SMS/WhatsApp — the license-expiry sweep has no customer.deletedAt filter, refuting the build plan's sweep claim that only the two fixed crons are customer-owned schedules.
findings.detail: `runExpirySweep` (@LeaderCron("0 3 * * *"), :57) runs per ACTIVE tenant and calls processTenant, which reads `forTenant().customerAuthorization.findMany({ where: { status: "VERIFIED", expiresAt: { lt: now } } })` at :100 and `{ status: "VERIFIED", expiresAt: { gte: now, lt: now+31d } }` at :141 — neither carries `customer: { deletedAt: null }`. For each matching row it calls `this.notify(...)` → :203 `notifications.sendToCustomer(auth.customerId, ...)` → notifications.service.ts:178-183 resolves the customer's userId with no status/deletedAt filter → sendToUser (:93-116) reads every DeviceToken for that user (soft delete deletes no tokens) and pushes; and `messaging.notifyEvent(NotificationEvent.LICENSE_EXPIRING, { customerId })` at :126 and :167 → messaging.service.ts:264-288 → notify (:195-236) → sendMessage (:85-122), which resolves the customer by id (`db.customer.findFirst({ where: { id: customerId } })`, no deletedAt filter) and sends over every enabled channel (EMAIL / SMS / WHATSAPP). Failure scenario: a tenant removes customer C on 2026-09-10 while C holds a VERIFIED tobacco licence expiring 2026-10-05. At 03:00 on 2026-09-11 the 30-day bucket fires: C's business email/phone receives "License expiring in 30 day(s)…" plus a push, and the sweep repeats for the 7-day and 1-day buckets and once more at the VERIFIED→EXPIRED flip (each bucket is once-only via expiringSoonNotifiedBucket, so up to four messages after removal). This is R2's exact prohibition ("never generate, and so never email") in a module nobody enrolled, and it is recorded nowhere: build-plan.md's Sibling notes end with "Sweep result at master … only the two fixed crons are customer-owned schedules", which is false — the sweep's own pattern (`isActive: true, (daysOfWeek|nextRunAt)`, pipeline-args.json siblingPatterns) structurally cannot match `status: "VERIFIED", expiresAt: …`, which is why the gap survived every file-scoped lens.

At minimum, correct the build plan's sweep claim and record this as a follow-up row.
findings.decision: The evidence traces a concrete send chain (customerAuthorization findMany with no customer filter -> sendToCustomer/notifyEvent -> push, email, SMS) that contacts a removed customer daily, which is exactly B131's symptom class and directly refutes the plan's sweep claim that only two crons are customer-owned.

findings.summary: Route dispatch still puts a removed customer on the driver's run, and this diff's new driver-branch refusal in OrdersService.create then fails the at-stop order with "Customer not found" — a live-operations dead end recorded nowhere.
findings.detail: The soft delete leaves RouteStop/RouteCustomer rows intact (customers.service.ts:2044-2047 writes only Customer.deletedAt + User INACTIVE; only mergeCustomers and batchDelete touch route rows, and both hard-delete instead). `createRun` reads `forTenant().route.findUnique({ include: { stops: { orderBy: { stopNumber: "asc" } } } })` at :808-811 with no customer filter and then creates a RouteRunStop for EVERY stop at :917-925 (`stops: { create: route.stops.map(s => ({ … customerId: s.customerId … })) }`). routes.service.ts contains no occurrence of `deletedAt` at all (verified by grep). Failure scenario: customer C is on scheduled route R; the operator removes C on Monday; on Tuesday the operator dispatches R and the driver's run still contains C's stop with C's business name and address (getLiveRoutes at :735-750 includes `customer: { select: { businessName: true } }`, so C is rendered normally). The driver drives to C and creates the order at the stop — POST /orders with role DRIVER — and now hits the new gate added by this diff (orders.service.ts:1734-1735, `if (customer.deletedAt) throw new BadRequestException("Customer not found")`), so the driver is told the shop they are standing in front of does not exist. Before this diff the order succeeded. So B131's "standing schedule keeps firing" shape survives in the routes module (never mentioned in build-plan.md's Sibling notes or its sweep result), and the diff's own sibling fix converts it from a silent wrong delivery into a driver-facing phantom error with no explanation.
findings.fixHint: Decide the intended end state for route assignments on removal and either (a) filter removed customers out of dispatch (add `customer: { deletedAt: null }` to the stops include at :809-811, or skip them in the :917-925 create) and surface a count the way the two crons now log their suppressed sets, or (b) keep dispatching and give the driver branch a distinguishable message. Either way record it — today neither the route nor the driver error mentions removal.

findings.summary: The third branch of the same OrdersService.create was not enrolled: a CUSTOMER-role user ordering for themselves resolves their customer row with no deletedAt check, so a removed customer can still place an order (and thus be invoiced) for the life of their access token.
findings.detail: The sibling fix added `if (customer.deletedAt) throw new BadRequestException("Customer not found")` to the staff branch (:1721) and the driver branch (:1735), but the self-service branch at :1738-1743 still does `forTenant().customer.findFirst({ where: { userId: user.sub } })` and only rejects `!customer`. Reachability is bounded but real: removal sets User.status = INACTIVE (customers.service.ts:2046), and login refuses non-ACTIVE (auth.service.ts:61) and refresh refuses it too (auth.service.ts:245-248) — but JwtStrategy.validate (auth/strategies/jwt.strategy.ts:21-30) never re-reads the User row, so an already-issued access token keeps working until it expires (JWT_EXPIRES_IN default "15m", config/configuration.ts:112). Failure scenario: a CUSTOMER-role user has the web/mobile ordering screen open; the operator removes them; within the remaining token lifetime the user submits their cart; the order is created for a removed customer, and createInvoiceFromOrder is explicitly in-bounds per the plan, so that order is then legitimately invoiceable — the exact outcome the staff/driver gate was added to prevent. build-plan.md's Sibling notes state "The customer-role branch … untouched" without saying why it is safe.
findings.fixHint: Either add the same `deletedAt` refusal to the branch at :1738-1743 (its existing ForbiddenException("Customer record not found") is the natural shape, keeping the message unchanged), or record in the plan why a 15-minute post-removal window on the self-order path is acceptable.
findings.decision: Two of three branches of the same create() were enrolled and the self-service branch was not; reachability is bounded to the remaining access-token lifetime (~15m) because login and refresh already refuse INACTIVE users, so it is an inconsistency worth closing, not a blocker.

findings.summary: Restoring a removed customer mints an immediate make-up recurring invoice — and auto-emails it — on the next midnight tick, a money write the plan's "restore-symmetric, no other write" framing never mentions.
findings.detail: The new filter at :403 suppresses due rows while the customer is removed and deliberately leaves nextRunAt untouched ("a restored customer's schedule resumes on its own"). But generateInvoiceFromTemplate's B46 advance is `advanceFrom = dueAt > now ? dueAt : now` (:237-239), i.e. a backlogged template is billed ONCE on selection and re-scheduled into the future. Failure scenario: MONTHLY template, dayOfMonth 1, nextRunAt 2026-07-01, autoSend true. Customer removed 2026-06-15; the 07-01, 08-01 and 09-01 ticks skip it (filter) and nextRunAt stays 2026-07-01. Operator restores the customer on 2026-09-20 (Undo or POST /customers/:id/restore). At 00:00 on 2026-09-21 the row is due again, generateInvoiceFromTemplate claims it, advances nextRunAt to 2026-10-01, mints a full monthly invoice dated today via invoicesService.create, and — because autoSend is set — emails it to the customer (:325-327). So "restore" is not a pure re-enable: it produces one immediate customer-visible invoice and email for a cycle the fix intentionally skipped. R6, the objective ("resumes with no other write") and acceptance criterion 6 ("the diff contains no writes") are all literally true of the diff while the composed behavior bills the customer the moment they are restored; no test or plan line covers it, and the suppression warning added in round 2 gives no hint that a make-up invoice is pending.
findings.fixHint: Decide the intended resume semantics and record it: either accept the single make-up invoice (then say so in the plan, and consider mentioning the pending catch-up in the suppression warning), or, if a removal window must not be billed at all, advance nextRunAt past the missed cycles on resume rather than billing one — a behavior change that needs an owner ruling since it also changes deactivate/activate (B46).
findings.decision: The B46 advance rule means a template suppressed during removal is billed once and auto-emailed on the first tick after restore; that is a plausible intended 'resume' semantic, but it is an undocumented money write on the restore path the plan frames as write-free, so it needs a documented decision rather than a silent default.

findings.summary: GoogleOAuthService.acceptInviteToken is the Google twin of the invite path this run gated, and it still redeems a removed customer's invite — writing the link ACTIVE and destroying the invite token irreversibly.
findings.detail:
Evidence. `acceptInviteToken` (google-oauth.service.ts:643-663) reads `this.prisma.customerLink.findFirst({ where: { inviteToken: token, status: { in: ["INVITED","PENDING_SELLER_APPROVAL"] } } })` at line 648 — no `customer: { deletedAt: null }` — and then at 652-661 writes `customerLink.update({ where: { id: link.id }, data: { buyerAccountId, status: "ACTIVE", inviteToken: null, inviteExpiresAt: null, linkedAt: new Date() } })`. It is called at line 610 of the same file from the Google sign-in flow whenever `profile.inviteToken` is present (the seller's invite email carries the token through OAuth state). The round-2 fence amendment edited THIS file 29 lines above (sellerCount at 618-620) and left this untouched; the new google-oauth.removed-customer.spec.ts covers only sellerCount (its two test titles are REG-B141 T11 and B141 P9 — verified by grep).

Failure scenario. Seller invites customer C (CustomerLink INVITED, inviteToken T emailed). Seller removes C — `CustomersService.deleteCustomer` soft branch (customers.service.ts:2044-2048) writes only `Customer.deletedAt` + `User.status=INACTIVE` and never touches the link. The buyer clicks the emailed invite and picks "Continue with Google": acceptInviteToken matches the link, flips it ACTIVE, binds buyerAccountId and NULLs inviteToken/inviteExpiresAt. The identical action via password sign-in goes through `BuyerService.acceptInvite` (buyer.service.ts:120-131), which this run gated with `customer: { deletedAt: null }` and which now 404s with no write (pinned by REG-B141 T10) — so the same invite link succeeds or fails purely by sign-in method.

Why it matters beyond cosmetics. (a) It is a CustomerLink write for a removed customer: build-plan R6 (lines ~46-52) states "There are no isActive writes, no CustomerLink writes" for the fixed paths, and the Sibling notes admit exactly one exception (`customers.service.ts approveBuyerRequest`). This is a second, undocumented one. (b) It is strictly worse than that exception because it CONSUMES the invite: after `restoreCustomer` (customers.service.ts:1965-1983 — verified to clear `deletedAt` and set `User.status` back to ACTIVE/SUSPENDED, with no CustomerLink write, so every other fixed path is genuinely restore-symmetric) the seller's outstanding invite token is gone and the link's buyerAccountId is whoever happened to click. Nothing restores it. (c) Within the same response, `sellerCount` (line 618, now filtered) returns 0, so the mobile client shows "not connected to any supplier" while the DB holds a fresh ACTIVE link — exactly the inconsistency class the round-2 amendment claims to have fixed.
findings.fixHint: Add `customer: { deletedAt: null }` to the where at google-oauth.service.ts:648 (the method already returns silently when no link matches, so no new error shape is needed), and pin it with a REG-B141 test in google-oauth.removed-customer.spec.ts asserting `customerLink.update` is never called for a removed customer's token.
findings.decision: Line 648 reads the CustomerLink by inviteToken with no customer.deletedAt filter and 652-661 writes status ACTIVE while nulling the token, so a removed customer's invite is redeemed irreversibly through the Google path; it is the exact twin of the already-confirmed acceptInvite/requestSeller finding and the round-2 fence edit in this same file (sellerCount) stopped 29 lines short of it, with the new spec covering only sellerCount.

findings.summary: The nightly authorization-expiry cron still pushes, WhatsApps/SMSes and emails a removed customer (metered to the seller) and consumes their warning buckets — the third customer-reaching @LeaderCron, and the only one the run never swept.
findings.detail:
Cron sweep (focused item #1), from `grep -rn "@LeaderCron" src` plus a check that no other scheduler exists (`@Interval`/`@Timeout`/`setInterval(` return zero non-spec hits): the 13 jobs are authorization-expiry.runExpirySweep, billing-cron.expireTrials/expireGrace/applyScheduledDowngrades/applyScheduledCancellations/rollCycles, billing.suspendOverdueTenants, order-templates.generateDailyOrders, orders.cronSweepPendingOrders, recurring-invoices.generateDueRecurringInvoices, regulated-filing.autoPrepareClosedFilings, commission-reconciliation.reconcileCommissions, tobacco-report.generateMonthlyReports — the same set no-bare-cron.spec.ts:20-33 pins. Of these, exactly three reach a customer: the two this run fixed, and authorization-expiry.runExpirySweep (line 57, "0 3 * * *"). The other ten contain no `sendToCustomer`/`notifyEvent` (grep on regulated-filing-cron, tobacco-report, commission-reconciliation: zero email/notifications/messaging hits; billing-* are tenant-level; orders.cronSweepPendingOrders only calls sweepAllPendingOrders, a merge with no send). There is NO invoice overdue/dunning cron at all: the only reminder sender is the operator-triggered `POST /invoices/:id/send-reminder` (invoices.controller.ts:209 → invoices.service.ts:3940), which is consistent with the plan's documented "invoicing already-delivered work is legitimate receivables" allowance.

Evidence in the unswept cron. `processTenant` reads `customerAuthorization.findMany` at line 100 (VERIFIED, expiresAt < now) and line 141 (expiring within 31 days) with no `customer: { deletedAt: null }`. Per row it then (1) calls `notify()` → `notifications.sendToCustomer(auth.customerId, subject, body)` at line 203; `NotificationsService.sendToCustomer` (notifications.service.ts:172-184) resolves `customer.findFirst({ where: { id } , select: { userId } })` with no deletedAt filter and pushes to the removed customer's still-registered device tokens; and (2) calls `messaging.notifyEvent(NotificationEvent.LICENSE_EXPIRING, { customerId })` at lines 126 and 167 → messaging.service.ts:260 → `notify()` (194) → `sendMessage()` (85), whose customer read at 92-103 also has no deletedAt filter, so the message goes out on every ENABLED channel (WhatsApp/SMS/EMAIL), is metered to the tenant (`meter.increment(tenantId, MeterKey.MSGS, 1)`, ~181) and writes a Message row + thread bump.

Failure scenario. Seller removes customer C on Sep 1 (Customer.deletedAt set; C's standing orders and recurring invoices are now correctly suppressed by this run's fix). C's licence expires Sep 5. At 03:00 on Sep 5 the sweep flips the authorization to EXPIRED, pushes "License expired: <category>" to C's phone, sends C the LICENSE_EXPIRING template over WhatsApp/SMS/email on the seller's metered quota, and emails the seller's own operators about a customer they deleted. The 30/7/1 warning path (line 141) does the same before expiry.

Restore asymmetry. The sweep also writes the removed customer's rows while removed: `customerAuthorization.update({ status: "EXPIRED", expiryNotifiedAt })` (~106) and `{ expiringSoonNotifiedBucket: bucket }` (~155), plus an audit row. Because `last <= bucket` skips an already-stamped bucket (line ~152), a customer removed then restored never receives the 7-day/1-day warning that was consumed while they were removed — the opposite of the stateless, restore-symmetric property R6 claims for this defect class.

Same shape, not a cron (for the fixer's radius): `stock-alerts/stock-alert.service.ts:117` pushes "Back in stock" to a removed customer and first claims the alert (`status: NOTIFIED, notifiedAt`, ~110), so that alert is consumed and never re-fires after restore.
findings.fixHint: Add `customer: { deletedAt: null }` to both `customerAuthorization.findMany` where-clauses (lines 100 and 141) so a removed customer is neither notified nor bucket-stamped; decide explicitly whether the VERIFIED→EXPIRED flip should still happen for a removed customer (a status-only flip with the two sends skipped is the restore-symmetric option, since the licence really did expire). Pin with a REG spec asserting `notifications.sendToCustomer` and `messaging.notifyEvent` are not called for a removed customer. Treat stock-alert.service.ts:117 as the same fix if the owner widens the radius.
findings.decision: The sweep enumerates the 13 @LeaderCron jobs pinned by no-bare-cron.spec and shows authorization-expiry.runExpirySweep is the third and only unfixed customer-reaching cron, so a removed customer still receives push/SMS/WhatsApp/email metered to the seller and consumes warning buckets — the same defect class as B131 itself, not a new one.

findings.summary: Both schedule create() methods in the two files this run edited still accept a removed customer, so a new standing order / recurring invoice is accepted, listed, and can never fire — the new cron filters make it a permanent silent no-op.
findings.detail:
Evidence. `OrderTemplatesService.create` (order-templates.service.ts:129-134) reads `forTenant().customer.findUnique({ where: { id: dto.customerId } })` and rejects only `!customer` (line 134) — no `deletedAt` check. Its twin `RecurringInvoicesService.create` (recurring-invoices.service.ts:83-87) has the identical shape (`if (!customer) throw new NotFoundException("Customer not found")` at line 87). This run added `customer: { deletedAt: null }` to the cron read of BOTH services (order-templates.service.ts ~316, recurring-invoices.service.ts ~400), so anything created for a removed customer is unreachable by the only thing that would ever run it.

Reachability through the normal UI (not just a stale tab). `CustomersService.findOne` (customers.service.ts:448-457) has NO `deletedAt` filter — contrast `findAll`, which does (line 126, "Exclude soft-deleted customers (RF-197)") — so `/customers/<id>` still renders for a removed customer (bookmark, browser Back after the 8-second Undo toast expires, or a bell-notification deep link). That page's Standing Orders tab carries an "Add Standing Order" button (apps/web/app/(dashboard)/customers/[id]/page.tsx ~3405-3425, which POSTs via the `@/lib/api/order-templates` import at line 141).

Failure scenario. Operator removes customer C, then reopens C's detail page and adds a standing order for the last outstanding delivery. The API returns 201, the template appears in the list with C's business name and its weekdays, and `generateDailyOrders` never generates anything from it: the new relation filter drops it, and the only trace is the new per-tenant WARN `REG-B131: N standing-order template(s) suppressed — customer removed`, which is a server log, not a product surface. Identical for `POST /recurring-invoices`: the schedule is created with a `nextRunAt` that is never advanced and never billed.

Why this is a gap in this run rather than a pre-existing sibling. The run deliberately gated the money write in this same shape — `InvoicesService.create` now refuses a removed customer with the not-found 404 (R3, invoices.service.ts:345) — and the plan's Sibling notes enumerate the other unfiltered customer reads it chose to defer (estimates.service.ts create/convertToInvoice, credit-notes.service.ts ~310, import.service.ts ~941, manual generateOrder, createInvoiceFromOrder). Neither schedule `create()` appears anywhere in the plan — not in the fence, not in R1-R6, not in the Sibling notes — even though both live in the two files the run edited, and the run's own filters are what turn them into silent no-ops.
findings.fixHint: Add the same `if (customer.deletedAt) throw …` guard used by InvoicesService.create to order-templates.service.ts:134 (keep the existing BadRequestException message) and recurring-invoices.service.ts:87 (keep NotFoundException), reusing the missing-customer message so no customer state leaks; pin each with a REG-B131 test asserting `orderTemplate.create` / `recurringInvoice.create` is never called. If the owner instead wants these creates allowed, the deferral needs to be a written Sibling-note row, because today the behavior is undocumented.
findings.decision: Both create() methods reject only !customer (order-templates 134, recurring-invoices 87) while the cron reads now filter customer.deletedAt, and findOne has no deletedAt filter so the page is reachable; the result is an accepted, listed schedule that can never fire — an inconsistency with the invoice create() rule, but a silent no-op rather than a money or access defect.

findings.summary: The round-3 OrdersService.create fix covers only two of the method's three branches, so the plan's claim that "no new post-removal order can be created and then invoiced" is false for a customer-role session whose access token predates the removal.
findings.detail:
Evidence. `OrdersService.create` resolves the target customer in three branches (orders.service.ts:1708-1745). The staff branch got `if (customer.deletedAt) throw new BadRequestException("Customer not found")` (line 1723) and the DRIVER branch the same (line 1734). The third branch — "Customer creates their own order", lines 1738-1744 — resolves `forTenant().customer.findFirst({ where: { userId: user.sub } })` and checks only `!customer`, with no deletedAt test. The plan's Sibling note (build-plan lines ~757-762) states "`OrdersService.create` now refuses a removed customer on the staff and driver branches … so no new post-removal order can be created and then invoiced. The customer-role branch … untouched" — it records the omission but never argues the branch is unreachable, and the completeness claim in the same sentence does not hold.

Why the branch is reachable after removal. Removal writes `User.status = "INACTIVE"` (customers.service.ts:2047), but `JwtStrategy.validate` (apps/api/src/auth/strategies/jwt.strategy.ts:19-30) trusts the token payload and never re-reads the User row, so an access token minted before removal keeps working until it expires; only the next login (`auth.service.ts:61`, `if (user.status !== "ACTIVE") return null`) and the next refresh (`auth.service.ts:245`) see INACTIVE. Default lifetime is `JWT_EXPIRES_IN ?? "15m"` (apps/api/src/config/configuration.ts:112); prod may set it longer, which widens the window.

Failure scenario. A CUSTOMER-role user has the order screen open on the mobile/web customer app. The operator removes them (their standing orders and recurring invoices stop, their invoice create 404s). Within the remaining token life the customer taps Submit: POST /orders takes the third branch, resolves their own still-existing Customer row, and writes a real PENDING order for a removed customer — which lands in the operator's queue for a customer the customers list no longer shows, and which `createInvoiceFromOrder` will then invoice (the plan allows that only for orders placed BEFORE removal).

Unpinned. `git diff HEAD -- apps/api/src/orders/orders.service.spec.ts` adds exactly two REG-B131 tests, both driving `prisma.customer.findUnique` (the staff and driver branches); the self-serve branch uses `prisma.customer.findFirst` and is not exercised.
findings.fixHint: Either add the same `if (customer.deletedAt) throw …` to the self-serve branch at orders.service.ts:1741 (message: keep the existing ForbiddenException("Customer record not found") shape for that branch so no customer state leaks) with a REG-B131 spec driving `prisma.customer.findFirst`, or — if the owner wants it deferred — correct the Sibling note so it stops claiming no post-removal order can be created, and record the JwtStrategy token-window reason.
findings.decision: The customer-role branch (1738-1744) resolves by userId with no deletedAt test while the staff and driver branches got the guard, and the run itself records that B141 revokes no token, so a pre-removal customer token can still create an order until it expires; the plan's completeness claim is false but the window is bounded by token TTL.

confirmedFindings.summary: A second operator-reachable path creates a NEW invoice for a soft-deleted customer, bypassing the create() guard added for R3, and it is recorded nowhere in the plan (neither the scope fence nor Sibling notes).
confirmedFindings.detail: EstimatesService.convertToInvoice (apps/api/src/estimates/estimates.service.ts:257-310, reached by POST /estimates/:id/convert-to-invoice at estimates.controller.ts:48) writes `tx.invoice.create({ data: { customerId: est.customerId, status: "DRAFT", ... } })` with no customer lookup and no deletedAt check (verified: `grep -n deletedAt src/estimates/*.ts` returns nothing for the non-spec files). Failure scenario: remove customer X on web (soft branch sets Customer.deletedAt), then open X's ACCEPTED estimate and convert it. The estimate is still listed — findAll (~line 183-201) builds its `where` from customerId/status/date/search only, no customer.deletedAt filter — so this is normal-UI reachable, not just a raw API call. The estimate flips to CONVERTED and a new DRAFT invoice is minted for the removed customer: exactly the state R3 blocks on the InvoicesService.create path (which I verified now 404s, T4/T5 green). This does not violate any acceptance criterion — the plan deliberately fences scope to the owner's three B131 sites — but the plan's Objective presents InvoicesService.create as the manual-invoicing surface and its Sibling notes DO record the analogous unfixed paths (createInvoiceFromOrder as legitimate receivables, recurring 'generate now', manual generateOrder, google-oauth sellerCount). Estimate conversion is a third manual path of the same shape and is absent from that list, so it will not be picked up as a follow-up row unless recorded.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Do not widen this run's diff. Record it as a follow-up row in the plan's Sibling notes alongside the other manual paths, with the owner deciding whether converting a pre-removal ACCEPTED estimate is legitimate receivables (like createInvoiceFromOrder) or must 404 like create(). If it is later fixed, the check belongs on the estimate's customer row inside convertToInvoice's transaction, mirroring create()'s `if (!customer || customer.deletedAt)`. confirmedFindings.summary: requestSeller and acceptInvite never check customer.deletedAt, so a locked-out buyer gets success or "already connected" for a seller getSellers now hides and the guard 403s.
confirmedFindings.detail: State: customer C at seller S is soft-removed; its CustomerLink is still ACTIVE (the plan's premise). (a) C's buyer, now 403'd everywhere and no longer seeing S in the switcher, calls POST /buyer/request-seller to reconnect. The customer lookup at line 183-189 has no deletedAt filter, so it finds the removed row, then line 218-220 returns 409 "You are already connected to this seller" -- while GET /buyer/sellers returns nothing for S and every guarded route says "No active connection to this seller". Three contradictory answers; neither the buyer nor support can tell which is true. (b) With emailProven (a different buyer, or the same buyer whose link was DISCONNECTED before removal) the upsert at line 255-271 WRITES a new ACTIVE CustomerLink onto a soft-deleted customer, emits emitBuyerAutoLinked to the seller's operators (a realtime "buyer connected" toast for a customer they removed) and returns "Connected! You can now view your orders and invoices from this seller" -- after which getSellers hides it and all 45 guarded routes 403. (c) The unproven branch (line 302-345) writes a PENDING_SELLER_APPROVAL link, emails the seller and queues an approval for a removed customer, promising "You'll see them in your seller list once approved", which getSellers can no longer honour. acceptInvite (line 116-160) is the same shape: a pre-removal invite is still redeemable, flips the link ACTIVE and returns tenantSlug, which the web client stores as activeSeller. The plan's scope fence excludes these routes, so this is a follow-up row, not an in-run fix -- but it is not in the plan's Sibling notes and it is the door buyers will actually push on after deploy.

confirmedFindings.summary: The change makes "Remove customer" silently kill standing orders, recurring invoices and portal access, but the only in-product way to reverse it is the 8-second Undo toast.
confirmedFindings.detail: The whole safety story of this fix is restore symmetry (R6, "Restore (Undo, or the restore endpoint) reverses all of it immediately"). In the product, restore is wired ONLY to the undo callback of runUndoable at line 1990-1995 (useRestoreCustomer is referenced nowhere else in apps/web -- verified by grep); the customers list filters deletedAt: null (apps/api/src/customers/customers.service.ts:126), so a removed customer disappears from every list, and while findOne (customers.service.ts:448-457) does NOT filter deletedAt so the detail page is reachable by direct URL, that page renders no Restore control. Scenario: an operator mis-clicks Remove on a live customer and misses the 8-second toast. Before this change the damage was cosmetic (hidden from the list). After it: that customer's 06:00 template tick and 00:00 recurring tick stop firing, manual invoicing 404s, and their buyer is 403'd out of the portal -- and the only remedy is a hand-crafted POST /customers/:id/restore (or a DB write), which no operator can issue from the UI.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Before or with this landing, give the removal an in-product reversal: an archived/removed filter on the customers list plus a Restore action on the detail page for a customer with deletedAt set (the API endpoint already exists and is idempotent). Web work, so a separate PR is fine, but do not treat R6 as satisfied by the API endpoint alone.

confirmedFindings.summary: The new refusal emits no log, audit row or Sentry event, so the plan's stated monitoring ("watch 403 'No active connection to this seller' rates") has no source to read.
confirmedFindings.detail: The guard's only new outcome is throw ForbiddenException at line 55, reached now for a removed customer's ACTIVE link. Nothing records it: main.ts registers no request/status logging (grep of main.ts for use(/Logger/morgan/pino finds only helmet and the body parser), app.module.ts registers no APP_INTERCEPTOR or APP_FILTER (only APP_GUARDs), and the one catch-all filter, common/sentry-exception.filter.ts:13-14, captures only status >= 500. 2am scenario: a buyer calls support saying their orders and invoices vanished at seller S; the operator says they removed nobody. Railway logs contain no line for the refusal, Sentry has no event, and the API cannot distinguish this 403 from a DISCONNECTED link. Diagnosis requires a direct DB read of Customer.deletedAt. Compounding it, the plan drafted a read-only report to size the population this guard locks out at deploy (build-plan.md Data repair, B141 row) but deliberately does not run it, so the count of live buyers who lose access the moment this deploys is unknown going in.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Cheapest shape that keeps one query: select deletedAt with the other customer fields and check it on the returned row instead of in the where (the same L-081-style row check invoices.service.ts:346 uses), then logger.warn once with tenantId + customerId before throwing the unchanged ForbiddenException -- REG-B141 T6/T7 still pass, since they assert the exception and req.buyerCustomer, not the where shape. Separately, run the drafted B141 read-only report before the deploy window so the blast radius is a number, not a guess.

confirmedFindings.summary: A removed customer can still be invoiced through estimate conversion, which bypasses the new InvoicesService.create guard entirely.

It never reads Customer and never touches InvoicesService.create (grep confirms create()'s only non-spec callers are invoices.controller.ts:53 and recurring-invoices.service.ts:266), so the R3 404 does not apply. Scenario: an ACCEPTED estimate exists for customer C; C is removed; an operator opens the estimates list (unfiltered by customer deletedAt) and clicks Convert -> a real invoice with a burned invoice number is created for a removed customer, the exact symptom R3 claims to close. Note this may be a deliberate parallel to createInvoiceFromOrder (committed work is legitimate receivables), which the plan fenced out on purpose -- so it needs a ruling, not a reflex fix.

confirmedFindings.summary: The buyer client restores activeSeller from localStorage and never reconciles it against the fetched sellers list, so a removed buyer lands on a wall of unexplained 403s on their last-used seller.
confirmedFindings.detail: The plan's Risks table left this for the reviewer to note; it is reachable. On mount, buyer-auth-context.tsx:46-52 sets activeSeller from localStorage and only refreshes the sellers list in the background, never dropping an activeSeller that has disappeared from that list. buyer-api-client.ts:19-32 keeps attaching X-Tenant-Slug from that stored object on every request, so every guarded query 403s; the portal pages redirect to /buyer/portal only when activeSeller is null (e.g. dashboard/page.tsx:195), which it is not. Scenario: seller S removes customer C at 09:00; C's buyer reloads their dashboard tab and sees error states across every card with no message that access was withdrawn. They are not bricked -- the 403 is not treated as an auth failure (buyer-api-client.ts:54 refreshes on 401 only, so other wholesalers keep working, and /buyer/portal is a picker that renders "No sellers connected yet"), but nothing in the UI tells them what happened or steers them back to the picker.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: When the sellers list resolves, clear activeSeller (and its stored copy) if its linkId is no longer present, then let the existing !activeSeller redirect send the buyer to /buyer/portal; ideally show a one-line "this seller ended your portal access" notice. Web-only follow-up, out of this run's fence.

confirmedFindings.summary: R3's "a removed customer cannot be invoiced" gate is bypassable: EstimatesService.create accepts a soft-deleted customer and convertToInvoice mints the invoice with a direct tx.invoice.create, never through the newly-guarded InvoicesService.create.
confirmedFindings.detail: Verified by reading the file at this worktree: `create()` (lines 46-49) reads `forTenant().customer.findUnique({ where: { id: dto.customerId } })` and only rejects `!customer` — no `deletedAt` check, unlike the fixed `InvoicesService.create` (invoices.service.ts:348). `convertToInvoice` (lines 257-345) writes the invoice itself at line ~307 (`tx.invoice.create({ data: { customerId: est.customerId, ... } })`) and does not call `InvoicesService.create`. Failure scenario: operator removes customer C (soft delete, `deletedAt` set); with C's id (stale page, saved URL, mobile cache, API client) they POST /estimates for C — accepted — mark it ACCEPTED, then POST the convert endpoint. A real numbered Invoice row for the removed customer C is created, which is exactly the outcome R3 forbids and T4/T5 pin only for the `InvoicesService.create` path. The plan's Sibling notes list does not mention estimates at all, so this second invoice-minting site is neither fixed nor recorded.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Either add the same row-level guard to EstimatesService.create/convertToInvoice (`if (!customer || customer.deletedAt) throw new NotFoundException("Customer not found")`, and re-read the customer at convert time), or — if the owner's three-site fence stands — add estimates (and credit-notes.service.ts:310, which has the same unfiltered customer read) to the build plan's Sibling notes as follow-up rows so R3's partial coverage is recorded rather than implied.

confirmedFindings.summary: requestSeller still matches a removed customer, so a buyer can (re)connect to one: it writes an ACTIVE/PENDING CustomerLink and notifies the seller, which contradicts R6's "no other write while removed" and leaves a dead portal the new guard silently refuses.
confirmedFindings.detail: Verified by reading buyer.service.ts 160-365: `requestSeller` looks up the seller-side customer with `this.prisma.customer.findFirst({ where: { tenantId, OR: [{ email }, { user: { email } }] } })` (line 183) — no `deletedAt: null`. If the sign-in email is proven it then `customerLink.upsert(... status: "ACTIVE", linkedAt: now, inviteToken: null ...)` (lines 250-271) and emits `emitBuyerAutoLinked`; if unproven it writes `PENDING_SELLER_APPROVAL` (lines 300-325), emails the seller (`notifySellerOfRequest`) and emits `emitBuyerConnectRequest`. The seller-side approval path has no deletedAt guard either (customers.service.ts:2735 `approveBuyerRequest` — `customerLink.findFirst({ where: { customerId, tenantId } })` then writes `status: "ACTIVE"`), and customers.service.ts:2780 `listPendingPortalApprovals` will show the request for a customer the seller already removed. Failure scenarios: (a) buyer whose customer record was removed calls POST /buyer/sellers/request with a proven email — gets "Connected! You can now view your orders and invoices from this seller", yet every seller-scoped route 403s ("No active connection to this seller") and getSellers hides the seller, so the portal is a dead end with a success message; (b) the removed customer's link row is rewritten (buyerAccountId/status/linkedAt overwritten, any inviteToken cleared), so a later restoreCustomer() no longer restores the prior portal state — the plan's R6 claim ("restore brings back every behavior with no other write") no longer holds for the CustomerLink; (c) the seller gets an email/bell request for a customer they deleted. No work package or Sibling note covers this path.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add `deletedAt: null` to the customer lookup in requestSeller (making it a 404 "No customer account found with that email at this seller"), and/or refuse approveBuyerRequest for a removed customer; at minimum record both, plus listPendingPortalApprovals, in the build plan's Sibling notes and drop the unqualified "no other write while removed" wording from R6.

confirmedFindings.summary: OrdersService.create still accepts a soft-deleted customer (it checks only user.status === "SUSPENDED", while removal writes INACTIVE), and createInvoiceFromOrder is explicitly in-bounds — so new orders and their invoices can still be produced for a removed customer.
confirmedFindings.detail: Verified by reading orders.service.ts 1701-1735: the staff branch reads `forTenant().customer.findUnique({ where: { id: dto.customerId }, include: { user: { select: { status: true } } } })`, rejects only `!customer` and `customer.user.status === "SUSPENDED"` (line 1716-1718). CustomersService.deleteCustomer's soft branch writes `User.status = "INACTIVE"` (per the plan, customers.service.ts ~2039-2049), which that check does not catch; the driver branch (1721-1727) checks nothing beyond existence. Failure scenario: operator removes customer C, then a stale customer-detail page or a queued mobile/API request posts an order with C's id — the order is created, and because the plan explicitly keeps `createInvoiceFromOrder` in bounds ("invoicing already-delivered work is legitimate receivables"), that post-removal order can be invoiced, reaching the same end state R3 blocks on the manual path. The plan's Sibling notes cover manual order-template generation but not OrdersService.create, so this sibling is unrecorded.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Decide explicitly: either reject `customer.deletedAt` in OrdersService.create's staff and driver branches (same BadRequest as "Customer not found"), or add it to the build plan's Sibling notes as a follow-up row and note that createInvoiceFromOrder's allowance only covers orders placed before removal.

confirmedFindings.summary: Templates and recurring invoices suppressed by the new relation filter are invisible in the cron summaries -- they are not even counted as skipped.
confirmedFindings.detail: generateDailyOrders' summary log (line 351) reports totalCreated/totalSkipped, but a template dropped by the new where clause never enters the loop, so it lands in neither counter: a tenant whose only due template belongs to a removed customer logs "0 created, 0 skipped", identical to a day with no templates at all. recurring-invoices.service.ts:402 is worse: with the removed customer filtered out, due.length becomes 0 and the function returns before the per-tenant log (line 408), so that tenant produces no line whatsoever, and the global summary (line 424) reports 0 generated. confirmedFindings.fixHint: Emit the suppressed count once per tenant per tick. Either keep the filter and log a single count of the excluded set (one extra cheap count per tenant per day, on a cron path, not a request path), or fetch as before and skip in-loop with totalSkipped++ plus a warn naming customerId -- REG-B131 T1/T2/T3 and P1/P2 pass either way, since they assert which templates reached createOrderFromTemplate / invoicesService.create, not the where shape.

remainingFindings.summary: The change makes "Remove customer" silently kill standing orders, recurring invoices and portal access, but the only in-product way to reverse it is the 8-second Undo toast.

remainingFindings.summary: A THIRD invite-redemption path — GoogleOAuthService.acceptInviteToken — was never enrolled in round 1's removed-customer gate, so a removed customer's invite is still redeemable via Google sign-in: it flips the link ACTIVE and permanently burns the invite token.

Consequences, all verified in code: (a) a removed customer's link goes ACTIVE, the write R6 and the round-1 fence amendment exist to prevent (the plan records only customers.service.ts approveBuyerRequest as an out-of-fence twin, and google-oauth.service.ts was admitted INTO scope by the round-2 amendment); (b) the invite token is nulled, which restore cannot undo — the seller must mint a new invite, so it is not restore-symmetric; (c) the same request then computes the newly-filtered `sellerCount` at :618 → 0, while auth.controller.ts:337 sets `linked: profile.inviteToken ? "true" : "false"` unconditionally, so the callback (web/(auth)/auth/google/callback/page.tsx:147) sends the buyer to /buyer/portal?linked=true and portal/page.tsx:332-360 shows "Seller connected successfully. Welcome!" over a seller list that getSellers now hides. Reachability beyond the race (page loaded while C was live, seller removes C during the Google round-trip, or a tab left open): GET /api/v1/auth/google?tenant=<slug>&context=portal&invite_token=<T> is unauthenticated, so a buyer holding their own emailed token can re-redeem it after removal.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Add the same relation filter used by BuyerService.acceptInvite to the findFirst at google-oauth.service.ts:647 (`customer: { deletedAt: null }`) so a removed customer's token is treated as not found (the method already `return`s silently on no match, so no new error shape). While there, consider that `linked` at auth.controller.ts:337 is derived from the presence of the token rather than from a successful redemption, so it will still claim "connected" after the skip.

Same state, third unenrolled path, distinct from the already-listed sellerCount minor.

remainingFindings.summary: A fourth customer-owned daily cron keeps contacting removed customers by push, email and SMS/WhatsApp — the license-expiry sweep has no customer.deletedAt filter, refuting the build plan's sweep claim that only the two fixed crons are customer-owned schedules.
remainingFindings.detail: `runExpirySweep` (@LeaderCron("0 3 * * *"), :57) runs per ACTIVE tenant and calls processTenant, which reads `forTenant().customerAuthorization.findMany({ where: { status: "VERIFIED", expiresAt: { lt: now } } })` at :100 and `{ status: "VERIFIED", expiresAt: { gte: now, lt: now+31d } }` at :141 — neither carries `customer: { deletedAt: null }`. For each matching row it calls `this.notify(...)` → :203 `notifications.sendToCustomer(auth.customerId, ...)` → notifications.service.ts:178-183 resolves the customer's userId with no status/deletedAt filter → sendToUser (:93-116) reads every DeviceToken for that user (soft delete deletes no tokens) and pushes; and `messaging.notifyEvent(NotificationEvent.LICENSE_EXPIRING, { customerId })` at :126 and :167 → messaging.service.ts:264-288 → notify (:195-236) → sendMessage (:85-122), which resolves the customer by id (`db.customer.findFirst({ where: { id: customerId } })`, no deletedAt filter) and sends over every enabled channel (EMAIL / SMS / WHATSAPP). Failure scenario: a tenant removes customer C on 2026-09-10 while C holds a VERIFIED tobacco licence expiring 2026-10-05. At 03:00 on 2026-09-11 the 30-day bucket fires: C's business email/phone receives "License expiring in 30 day(s)…" plus a push, and the sweep repeats for the 7-day and 1-day buckets and once more at the VERIFIED→EXPIRED flip (each bucket is once-only via expiringSoonNotifiedBucket, so up to four messages after removal). This is R2's exact prohibition ("never generate, and so never email") in a module nobody enrolled, and it is recorded nowhere: build-plan.md's Sibling notes end with "Sweep result at master … only the two fixed crons are customer-owned schedules", which is false — the sweep's own pattern (`isActive: true, (daysOfWeek|nextRunAt)`, pipeline-args.json siblingPatterns) structurally cannot match `status: "VERIFIED", expiresAt: …`, which is why the gap survived every file-scoped lens.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Either add `customer: { deletedAt: null }` to both customerAuthorization reads (:100 and :141 — stateless and restore-symmetric like the two fixed crons, though it also stops the VERIFIED→EXPIRED status flip, so decide whether the flip should still happen silently while the notification is suppressed), or suppress only the two customer-facing sends (notifications.sendToCustomer at :203 and messaging.notifyEvent at :126/:167) and keep operator notices. At minimum, correct the build plan's sweep claim and record this as a follow-up row.

remainingFindings.summary: Restoring a removed customer mints an immediate make-up recurring invoice — and auto-emails it — on the next midnight tick, a money write the plan's "restore-symmetric, no other write" framing never mentions.
remainingFindings.detail: The new filter at :403 suppresses due rows while the customer is removed and deliberately leaves nextRunAt untouched ("a restored customer's schedule resumes on its own"). But generateInvoiceFromTemplate's B46 advance is `advanceFrom = dueAt > now ? dueAt : now` (:237-239), i.e. a backlogged template is billed ONCE on selection and re-scheduled into the future. Failure scenario: MONTHLY template, dayOfMonth 1, nextRunAt 2026-07-01, autoSend true. Customer removed 2026-06-15; the 07-01, 08-01 and 09-01 ticks skip it (filter) and nextRunAt stays 2026-07-01. Operator restores the customer on 2026-09-20 (Undo or POST /customers/:id/restore). At 00:00 on 2026-09-21 the row is due again, generateInvoiceFromTemplate claims it, advances nextRunAt to 2026-10-01, mints a full monthly invoice dated today via invoicesService.create, and — because autoSend is set — emails it to the customer (:325-327). So "restore" is not a pure re-enable: it produces one immediate customer-visible invoice and email for a cycle the fix intentionally skipped. R6, the objective ("resumes with no other write") and acceptance criterion 6 ("the diff contains no writes") are all literally true of the diff while the composed behavior bills the customer the moment they are restored; no test or plan line covers it, and the suppression warning added in round 2 gives no hint that a make-up invoice is pending.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Decide the intended resume semantics and record it: either accept the single make-up invoice (then say so in the plan, and consider mentioning the pending catch-up in the suppression warning), or, if a removal window must not be billed at all, advance nextRunAt past the missed cycles on resume rather than billing one — a behavior change that needs an owner ruling since it also changes deactivate/activate (B46).
remainingFindings.decision: The B46 advance rule means a template suppressed during removal is billed once and auto-emailed on the first tick after restore; that is a plausible intended 'resume' semantic, but it is an undocumented money write on the restore path the plan frames as write-free, so it needs a documented decision rather than a silent default.

This is a second, distinct instance of the already-reported google-oauth spec gap: that finding names apps/api/src/auth/google-oauth.removed-customer.spec.ts; this one is apps/api/src/orders/orders.service.spec.ts, a different file added by a different fence amendment.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Add `src/orders/orders.service` (and `src/auth/google-oauth.removed-customer`) to the final verification command at build-plan.md:716 and to the mirrored string at :929, and add the orders.service.ts row to the mutation-probe table so the sibling fixes carry a revert probe like the five primary files.

remainingFindings.summary: GoogleOAuthService.acceptInviteToken is the Google twin of the invite path this run gated, and it still redeems a removed customer's invite — writing the link ACTIVE and destroying the invite token irreversibly.
remainingFindings.detail:
Evidence. `acceptInviteToken` (google-oauth.service.ts:643-663) reads `this.prisma.customerLink.findFirst({ where: { inviteToken: token, status: { in: ["INVITED","PENDING_SELLER_APPROVAL"] } } })` at line 648 — no `customer: { deletedAt: null }` — and then at 652-661 writes `customerLink.update({ where: { id: link.id }, data: { buyerAccountId, status: "ACTIVE", inviteToken: null, inviteExpiresAt: null, linkedAt: new Date() } })`. It is called at line 610 of the same file from the Google sign-in flow whenever `profile.inviteToken` is present (the seller's invite email carries the token through OAuth state). The round-2 fence amendment edited THIS file 29 lines above (sellerCount at 618-620) and left this untouched; the new google-oauth.removed-customer.spec.ts covers only sellerCount (its two test titles are REG-B141 T11 and B141 P9 — verified by grep).

Failure scenario. Seller invites customer C (CustomerLink INVITED, inviteToken T emailed). Seller removes C — `CustomersService.deleteCustomer` soft branch (customers.service.ts:2044-2048) writes only `Customer.deletedAt` + `User.status=INACTIVE` and never touches the link. The buyer clicks the emailed invite and picks "Continue with Google": acceptInviteToken matches the link, flips it ACTIVE, binds buyerAccountId and NULLs inviteToken/inviteExpiresAt. The identical action via password sign-in goes through `BuyerService.acceptInvite` (buyer.service.ts:120-131), which this run gated with `customer: { deletedAt: null }` and which now 404s with no write (pinned by REG-B141 T10) — so the same invite link succeeds or fails purely by sign-in method.

Why it matters beyond cosmetics. (a) It is a CustomerLink write for a removed customer: build-plan R6 (lines ~46-52) states "There are no isActive writes, no CustomerLink writes" for the fixed paths, and the Sibling notes admit exactly one exception (`customers.service.ts approveBuyerRequest`). This is a second, undocumented one. (b) It is strictly worse than that exception because it CONSUMES the invite: after `restoreCustomer` (customers.service.ts:1965-1983 — verified to clear `deletedAt` and set `User.status` back to ACTIVE/SUSPENDED, with no CustomerLink write, so every other fixed path is genuinely restore-symmetric) the seller's outstanding invite token is gone and the link's buyerAccountId is whoever happened to click. Nothing restores it. (c) Within the same response, `sellerCount` (line 618, now filtered) returns 0, so the mobile client shows "not connected to any supplier" while the DB holds a fresh ACTIVE link — exactly the inconsistency class the round-2 amendment claims to have fixed.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Add `customer: { deletedAt: null }` to the where at google-oauth.service.ts:648 (the method already returns silently when no link matches, so no new error shape is needed), and pin it with a REG-B141 test in google-oauth.removed-customer.spec.ts asserting `customerLink.update` is never called for a removed customer's token.
remainingFindings.decision: Line 648 reads the CustomerLink by inviteToken with no customer.deletedAt filter and 652-661 writes status ACTIVE while nulling the token, so a removed customer's invite is redeemed irreversibly through the Google path; it is the exact twin of the already-confirmed acceptInvite/requestSeller finding and the round-2 fence edit in this same file (sellerCount) stopped 29 lines short of it, with the new spec covering only sellerCount.

remainingFindings.summary: The nightly authorization-expiry cron still pushes, WhatsApps/SMSes and emails a removed customer (metered to the seller) and consumes their warning buckets — the third customer-reaching @LeaderCron, and the only one the run never swept.
remainingFindings.detail:
Cron sweep (focused item #1), from `grep -rn "@LeaderCron" src` plus a check that no other scheduler exists (`@Interval`/`@Timeout`/`setInterval(` return zero non-spec hits): the 13 jobs are authorization-expiry.runExpirySweep, billing-cron.expireTrials/expireGrace/applyScheduledDowngrades/applyScheduledCancellations/rollCycles, billing.suspendOverdueTenants, order-templates.generateDailyOrders, orders.cronSweepPendingOrders, recurring-invoices.generateDueRecurringInvoices, regulated-filing.autoPrepareClosedFilings, commission-reconciliation.reconcileCommissions, tobacco-report.generateMonthlyReports — the same set no-bare-cron.spec.ts:20-33 pins. Of these, exactly three reach a customer: the two this run fixed, and authorization-expiry.runExpirySweep (line 57, "0 3 * * *"). The other ten contain no `sendToCustomer`/`notifyEvent` (grep on regulated-filing-cron, tobacco-report, commission-reconciliation: zero email/notifications/messaging hits; billing-* are tenant-level; orders.cronSweepPendingOrders only calls sweepAllPendingOrders, a merge with no send). There is NO invoice overdue/dunning cron at all: the only reminder sender is the operator-triggered `POST /invoices/:id/send-reminder` (invoices.controller.ts:209 → invoices.service.ts:3940), which is consistent with the plan's documented "invoicing already-delivered work is legitimate receivables" allowance.

Evidence in the unswept cron. `processTenant` reads `customerAuthorization.findMany` at line 100 (VERIFIED, expiresAt < now) and line 141 (expiring within 31 days) with no `customer: { deletedAt: null }`. Per row it then (1) calls `notify()` → `notifications.sendToCustomer(auth.customerId, subject, body)` at line 203; `NotificationsService.sendToCustomer` (notifications.service.ts:172-184) resolves `customer.findFirst({ where: { id } , select: { userId } })` with no deletedAt filter and pushes to the removed customer's still-registered device tokens; and (2) calls `messaging.notifyEvent(NotificationEvent.LICENSE_EXPIRING, { customerId })` at lines 126 and 167 → messaging.service.ts:260 → `notify()` (194) → `sendMessage()` (85), whose customer read at 92-103 also has no deletedAt filter, so the message goes out on every ENABLED channel (WhatsApp/SMS/EMAIL), is metered to the tenant (`meter.increment(tenantId, MeterKey.MSGS, 1)`, ~181) and writes a Message row + thread bump.

Failure scenario. Seller removes customer C on Sep 1 (Customer.deletedAt set; C's standing orders and recurring invoices are now correctly suppressed by this run's fix). C's licence expires Sep 5. At 03:00 on Sep 5 the sweep flips the authorization to EXPIRED, pushes "License expired: <category>" to C's phone, sends C the LICENSE_EXPIRING template over WhatsApp/SMS/email on the seller's metered quota, and emails the seller's own operators about a customer they deleted. The 30/7/1 warning path (line 141) does the same before expiry.

Restore asymmetry. The sweep also writes the removed customer's rows while removed: `customerAuthorization.update({ status: "EXPIRED", expiryNotifiedAt })` (~106) and `{ expiringSoonNotifiedBucket: bucket }` (~155), plus an audit row. Because `last <= bucket` skips an already-stamped bucket (line ~152), a customer removed then restored never receives the 7-day/1-day warning that was consumed while they were removed — the opposite of the stateless, restore-symmetric property R6 claims for this defect class.

Same shape, not a cron (for the fixer's radius): `stock-alerts/stock-alert.service.ts:117` pushes "Back in stock" to a removed customer and first claims the alert (`status: NOTIFIED, notifiedAt`, ~110), so that alert is consumed and never re-fires after restore.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Add `customer: { deletedAt: null }` to both `customerAuthorization.findMany` where-clauses (lines 100 and 141) so a removed customer is neither notified nor bucket-stamped; decide explicitly whether the VERIFIED→EXPIRED flip should still happen for a removed customer (a status-only flip with the two sends skipped is the restore-symmetric option, since the licence really did expire). Pin with a REG spec asserting `notifications.sendToCustomer` and `messaging.notifyEvent` are not called for a removed customer. Treat stock-alert.service.ts:117 as the same fix if the owner widens the radius.
remainingFindings.decision: The sweep enumerates the 13 @LeaderCron jobs pinned by no-bare-cron.spec and shows authorization-expiry.runExpirySweep is the third and only unfixed customer-reaching cron, so a removed customer still receives push/SMS/WhatsApp/email metered to the seller and consumes warning buckets — the same defect class as B131 itself, not a new one.

remainingFindings.summary: Both schedule create() methods in the two files this run edited still accept a removed customer, so a new standing order / recurring invoice is accepted, listed, and can never fire — the new cron filters make it a permanent silent no-op.
remainingFindings.detail:
Evidence. `OrderTemplatesService.create` (order-templates.service.ts:129-134) reads `forTenant().customer.findUnique({ where: { id: dto.customerId } })` and rejects only `!customer` (line 134) — no `deletedAt` check. Its twin `RecurringInvoicesService.create` (recurring-invoices.service.ts:83-87) has the identical shape (`if (!customer) throw new NotFoundException("Customer not found")` at line 87). This run added `customer: { deletedAt: null }` to the cron read of BOTH services (order-templates.service.ts ~316, recurring-invoices.service.ts ~400), so anything created for a removed customer is unreachable by the only thing that would ever run it.

Reachability through the normal UI (not just a stale tab). `CustomersService.findOne` (customers.service.ts:448-457) has NO `deletedAt` filter — contrast `findAll`, which does (line 126, "Exclude soft-deleted customers (RF-197)") — so `/customers/<id>` still renders for a removed customer (bookmark, browser Back after the 8-second Undo toast expires, or a bell-notification deep link). That page's Standing Orders tab carries an "Add Standing Order" button (apps/web/app/(dashboard)/customers/[id]/page.tsx ~3405-3425, which POSTs via the `@/lib/api/order-templates` import at line 141).

Failure scenario. Operator removes customer C, then reopens C's detail page and adds a standing order for the last outstanding delivery. The API returns 201, the template appears in the list with C's business name and its weekdays, and `generateDailyOrders` never generates anything from it: the new relation filter drops it, and the only trace is the new per-tenant WARN `REG-B131: N standing-order template(s) suppressed — customer removed`, which is a server log, not a product surface. Identical for `POST /recurring-invoices`: the schedule is created with a `nextRunAt` that is never advanced and never billed.

Why this is a gap in this run rather than a pre-existing sibling. The run deliberately gated the money write in this same shape — `InvoicesService.create` now refuses a removed customer with the not-found 404 (R3, invoices.service.ts:345) — and the plan's Sibling notes enumerate the other unfiltered customer reads it chose to defer (estimates.service.ts create/convertToInvoice, credit-notes.service.ts ~310, import.service.ts ~941, manual generateOrder, createInvoiceFromOrder). Neither schedule `create()` appears anywhere in the plan — not in the fence, not in R1-R6, not in the Sibling notes — even though both live in the two files the run edited, and the run's own filters are what turn them into silent no-ops.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Add the same `if (customer.deletedAt) throw …` guard used by InvoicesService.create to order-templates.service.ts:134 (keep the existing BadRequestException message) and recurring-invoices.service.ts:87 (keep NotFoundException), reusing the missing-customer message so no customer state leaks; pin each with a REG-B131 test asserting `orderTemplate.create` / `recurringInvoice.create` is never called. If the owner instead wants these creates allowed, the deferral needs to be a written Sibling-note row, because today the behavior is undocumented.
remainingFindings.decision: Both create() methods reject only !customer (order-templates 134, recurring-invoices 87) while the cron reads now filter customer.deletedAt, and findOne has no deletedAt filter so the page is reachable; the result is an accepted, listed schedule that can never fire — an inconsistency with the invoice create() rule, but a silent no-op rather than a money or access defect.

remainingFindings.summary: The round-3 OrdersService.create fix covers only two of the method's three branches, so the plan's claim that "no new post-removal order can be created and then invoiced" is false for a customer-role session whose access token predates the removal.
remainingFindings.detail:
Evidence. `OrdersService.create` resolves the target customer in three branches (orders.service.ts:1708-1745). The staff branch got `if (customer.deletedAt) throw new BadRequestException("Customer not found")` (line 1723) and the DRIVER branch the same (line 1734). The third branch — "Customer creates their own order", lines 1738-1744 — resolves `forTenant().customer.findFirst({ where: { userId: user.sub } })` and checks only `!customer`, with no deletedAt test. The plan's Sibling note (build-plan lines ~757-762) states "`OrdersService.create` now refuses a removed customer on the staff and driver branches … so no new post-removal order can be created and then invoiced. The customer-role branch … untouched" — it records the omission but never argues the branch is unreachable, and the completeness claim in the same sentence does not hold.

Why the branch is reachable after removal. Removal writes `User.status = "INACTIVE"` (customers.service.ts:2047), but `JwtStrategy.validate` (apps/api/src/auth/strategies/jwt.strategy.ts:19-30) trusts the token payload and never re-reads the User row, so an access token minted before removal keeps working until it expires; only the next login (`auth.service.ts:61`, `if (user.status !== "ACTIVE") return null`) and the next refresh (`auth.service.ts:245`) see INACTIVE. Default lifetime is `JWT_EXPIRES_IN ?? "15m"` (apps/api/src/config/configuration.ts:112); prod may set it longer, which widens the window.

Failure scenario. A CUSTOMER-role user has the order screen open on the mobile/web customer app. The operator removes them (their standing orders and recurring invoices stop, their invoice create 404s). Within the remaining token life the customer taps Submit: POST /orders takes the third branch, resolves their own still-existing Customer row, and writes a real PENDING order for a removed customer — which lands in the operator's queue for a customer the customers list no longer shows, and which `createInvoiceFromOrder` will then invoice (the plan allows that only for orders placed BEFORE removal).

Unpinned. `git diff HEAD -- apps/api/src/orders/orders.service.spec.ts` adds exactly two REG-B131 tests, both driving `prisma.customer.findUnique` (the staff and driver branches); the self-serve branch uses `prisma.customer.findFirst` and is not exercised.
remainingFindings.fixHint: Either add the same `if (customer.deletedAt) throw …` to the self-serve branch at orders.service.ts:1741 (message: keep the existing ForbiddenException("Customer record not found") shape for that branch so no customer state leaks) with a REG-B131 spec driving `prisma.customer.findFirst`, or — if the owner wants it deferred — correct the Sibling note so it stops claiming no post-removal order can be created, and record the JwtStrategy token-window reason.
remainingFindings.decision: The customer-role branch (1738-1744) resolves by userId with no deletedAt test while the staff and driver branches got the guard, and the run itself records that B141 revokes no token, so a pre-removal customer token can still create an order until it expires; the plan's completeness claim is false but the window is bounded by token TTL.
